passages.text: For likewise the pairing connected with Elijah, though due to come, was willingly left behind until another time, having decided to take it up on another suitable occasion. Therefore the one “among those born of women” came first; then the one among the sons of men came second. By following this sequence, it was possible to understand whose Simon is—the one who, before me, was first to come to the Gentiles—and whose I am, I who have come after him and come upon him as light upon darkness, as knowledge upon ignorance, as healing upon disease. So then, just as the true prophet told us, a false gospel must first come from a certain deceiver, and only then, after the destruction of the holy place, must a true gospel be sent out secretly to set right the heresies that will arise. After these things, toward the end, the Antichrist must again come first, and then our Jesus, who is truly the Messiah, must appear; and after that, when eternal light has risen, everything belonging to darkness must disappear.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the pairing connected with Elijah
lexical_decisions.rationale: συζυγία denotes a conjunction or paired counterpart in the author’s sequence of paired figures; “connected with” leaves the precise relationship open.

lexical_decisions.chosen: to take it up on another suitable occasion
lexical_decisions.rationale: The referent of αὐτήν is not explicit. “Take it up” reflects ἀπολαβεῖν while allowing the pairing or its deferred fulfillment to be intended; “receive it” or “recover it” are possible alternatives.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τίνος ἐστὶν Σίμων, ὁ πρὸ ἐμοῦ εἰς τὰ ἔθνη πρῶτος ἐλθών, καὶ τίνος ὢν τυγχάνω
lexical_decisions.chosen: whose Simon is—the one who, before me, was first to come to the Gentiles—and whose I am
lexical_decisions.rationale: The repeated τίνος expresses affiliation or belonging within the paired sequence; specifying a particular owner, side, or spiritual source would resolve an ambiguity the Greek leaves open.

lexical_decisions.chosen: our Jesus, who is truly the Messiah
lexical_decisions.rationale: Χριστός functions as a title here, emphasized by ὄντως, rather than merely as part of a conventional personal name.

passages.text: Since, then, as I said, some people are ignorant of the rule of pairing, for this reason they do not know who Simon, the one who went ahead of me, actually is. For if he were known, he would not have been believed. But now, because he is unknown, he has wrongly been believed. The one who does what haters do has been loved; the enemy has been welcomed as a friend; though he is death, he has been desired as one who saves; though he is fire, he has been regarded as light; and though he is a deceiver, he is listened to as one who speaks the truth. When I, Clement, heard these things, I said, “Who, then, is this man, such a great deceiver? I would like to know.” Peter said, “If you wish to learn, it is within your reach to find out from those from whom I too accurately learned everything concerning him.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: the rule of pairing
lexical_decisions.rationale: κανών is the governing pattern or rule, while συζυγία continues the author’s technical language of paired figures.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the one who does what haters do
lexical_decisions.rationale: The Greek literally refers to doing “the things of those who hate.” This rendering preserves that unusual expression; “the deeds of hatred” is a smoother but less formally exact alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: though he is death, he has been desired as one who saves
lexical_decisions.rationale: The contrast identifies him with death and presents him as falsely desired in the role of a saving figure; “as a savior” would be an idiomatic alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: it is within your reach to find out
lexical_decisions.rationale: The expression states that the opportunity or means of knowing is available to Clement, not merely that knowledge is physically present.

passages.text: There is among us a certain Justa, a Syrophoenician and a Canaanite by ancestry, whose little daughter was afflicted by a severe disease. She approached our Lord, crying out and pleading that he heal her little daughter. But he, when appealed to by us as well, said, “It is not permitted to heal the Gentiles, who resemble dogs because they use different foods and practices, since the table corresponding to the royal one has been allotted to the sons of Israel.” When she heard this, wishing, like a dog, to partake as well of crumbs falling from that same table, she changed what she had been by living in the same way as the sons of the kingdom, and obtained, as she had requested, healing for her little daughter. For had she remained a Gentile—being a Gentile and continuing in the same way of life—he would not have healed her, since in the first place it was not permitted to heal her as a Gentile.

lexical_decisions.chosen: a Syrophoenician and a Canaanite by ancestry
lexical_decisions.rationale: The first term identifies her regional or ethnic designation, while τὸ γένος explicitly marks Canaanite descent or ancestry.

lexical_decisions.chosen: little daughter
lexical_decisions.rationale: The diminutive form is retained as “little daughter.” It may be affectionate or lexicalized rather than a precise statement of age.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὁ δὲ καὶ ὑφ’ ἡμῶν ἀξιωθεὶς
lexical_decisions.chosen: But he, when appealed to by us as well
lexical_decisions.rationale: In this context ἀξιωθείς describes his being petitioned or entreated by the disciples; the more literal “deemed worthy by us” would not fit the following response as naturally.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀποδεδομένης τῆς κατὰ τὴν βασίλειον τραπέζης τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραήλ
lexical_decisions.chosen: since the table corresponding to the royal one has been allotted to the sons of Israel
lexical_decisions.rationale: This provisionally retains τραπέζης as the head of the genitive absolute and takes τὴν βασίλειον substantivally or elliptically, with another “table” understood after it. The construction is unusual; a conjectural change of τραπέζης to τράπεζαν would instead support a sense such as “what belongs at the royal table,” but that is not the supplied reading.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ τῆς αὐτῆς τραπέζης ὡς κύων ψιχίων ἀποπιπτόντων συνμεταλαμβάνειν βουλομένη
lexical_decisions.chosen: wishing, like a dog, to partake as well of crumbs falling from that same table
lexical_decisions.rationale: συνμεταλαμβάνειν conveys sharing or partaking along with others, while the genitives associate the crumbs with their falling from the table.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μεταθεμένη ὅπερ ἦν, τῷ ὁμοίως διαιτᾶσθαι τοῖς τῆς βασιλείας .υἱοῖς
lexical_decisions.chosen: she changed what she had been by living in the same way as the sons of the kingdom
lexical_decisions.rationale: The articular infinitive with the dative article expresses the means by which the change occurred. διαιτᾶσθαι concerns manner of life, including the foods and practices just mentioned; the printed full stop before υἱοῖς is treated provisionally as non-syntactic punctuation and disclosed separately.

source_issues.source_quote: ἀποδεδομένης τῆς κατὰ τὴν βασίλειον τραπέζης τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραήλ.
source_issues.issue: The verified printed construction is unusual but permits a provisional unaltered-text analysis: τραπέζης can be the head of the genitive absolute, while τὴν βασίλειον is substantival or elliptical, with another “table” understood. Changing τραπέζης to τράπεζαν would produce a different construction and support an allotted portion or provisions at the royal table, but that remains a conjecture rather than the supplied reading.
source_issues.proposed_reading: ἀποδεδομένης τῆς κατὰ τὴν βασίλειον τράπεζαν τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραήλ.

source_issues.issue: The verified printed full stop interrupts the noun phrase. It is provisionally treated as non-syntactic or stray editorial punctuation because taking it as a sentence boundary does not yield a defensible construction here.

passages.text: This very woman, then, after adopting a way of life according to law, was driven from her own home, together with her healed daughter, by her own husband, who held opinions opposed to ours. But she, remaining faithful to her agreements and having abundant means, herself remained a widow, while she arranged her daughter’s marriage to a certain man who was favorably disposed toward the true faith and was poor. Then, being deprived also of her daughter because of the marriage, she bought two boys, educated them, and had them in place of sons. Having been educated together with Simon the magician from childhood, they learned thoroughly everything concerning him; for their friendship with him was so close that they were even closely joined to him in every matter in which he wished to unite with them.

lexical_decisions.chosen: after adopting a way of life according to law
lexical_decisions.rationale: πολιτεία denotes a manner of life or conduct, and νόμιμον connects it with law-observant practice rather than merely describing it as socially respectable.

lexical_decisions.chosen: remaining faithful to her agreements
lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase describes honorable fidelity toward established agreements, probably her marital commitments in context; “marriage covenant” is possible but more specific than the Greek itself.

lexical_decisions.chosen: being deprived also of her daughter because of the marriage
lexical_decisions.rationale: πρόφασις can indicate the occasion or stated reason, not necessarily a deceptive pretext. The sense is that the daughter’s marriage deprived Justa of her presence or companionship.

lexical_decisions.chosen: she bought two boys
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὠνησαμένη explicitly describes purchase, while the following statement that she treated them as sons supports taking παῖδας as boys rather than generically as children.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοσαύτη γὰρ αὐτῶν ἦν ἡ φιλία, ὡς καὶ συνοστεῦσαι αὐτῷ
lexical_decisions.chosen: for their friendship with him was so close that they were even closely joined to him
lexical_decisions.rationale: συνοστεῦσαι expresses close association or intimate attachment, more strongly than merely keeping company. “Were intimate with him” is possible but could carry an unintended sexual implication in modern English.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐν πᾶσιν οἷς βούλοιτο αὐτοῖς ἐνοῦν
lexical_decisions.chosen: in every matter in which he wished to unite with them
lexical_decisions.rationale: The rendering provisionally understands the printed ἐνοῦν as corresponding in sense to ἑνοῦν, “unite,” with αὐτοῖς identifying those with whom Simon wished to join. A conjectural alteration to αὐτοὺς ἐνεῖναι would instead mean “in everything in which he wished them to be present.”

source_issues.issue: The printed ἐνοῦν and its construction with οἷς and αὐτοῖς are unusual. It can defensibly be understood as corresponding in sense to ἑνοῦν, “to unite,” yielding “in every matter in which he wished to unite with them.” The alternative sense “in which he wished them to be present” requires the conjectural alteration αὐτοῖς ἐνοῦν to αὐτοὺς ἐνεῖναι and is not another reading of the unchanged words.
